endReason.MEMBER_LEFT: Expired because the owner left the workspace (older keys)
endReason.ENDPOINT_DELETED: Expired because the endpoint was deleted

list.label: MCP keys
list.auditAria: View {{name}}'s audit log in this workspace

expire.title: Expire key {{name}}?
expire.body: Once expired, this key can no longer connect. This can't be undone. The key isn't deleted; it stays in the issuance history.
expire.noteHelp: Recorded in the audit log. Up to 500 characters.
expire.already: This key had already expired. The list has been refreshed.

issue.title: Issue an MCP key
issue.body: An AI agent (such as Claude Code) uses this key to work on projects and issues for you. One key works in every workspace you belong to where your role includes "Work in this workspace with an MCP key", with exactly the permissions you have there. Everything it does is recorded in the audit log.
issue.name: Key name
issue.namePlaceholder: e.g. Claude Code on my laptop
issue.nameHelp: A name that tells you where this key is used. Up to 100 characters.
issue.nameTooLong: Key names can be up to 100 characters.
issue.periodHelp: The key expires automatically at the end of the period. Valid until {{date}}.
issue.notAllowed: There is no workspace you can work in with an MCP key. You need at least one workspace where your role includes "Work in this workspace with an MCP key". Ask a workspace admin if you need it.
issue.noWorkspace: You need to belong to a workspace to issue an MCP key. Join a workspace first.
issue.once: The key is shown only this once. Once you close this window you can't see it again, so copy it now and keep it somewhere safe. If you lose it, expire this key and issue a new one.
issue.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
issue.allWorkspaces: One key works in every workspace you belong to; you don't pick a workspace. Only workspaces where your role includes "Work in this workspace with an MCP key" are visible, and if the same project name exists in several workspaces, the agent names the workspace too.
issue.projectNote: The same key also connects to the project management endpoint. It lists projects and manages per-type issue templates; management tasks such as creating or deleting projects will be added here. What the key can do follows its owner's permissions.
issue.claudeCode: Command to register the issue endpoint in Claude Code
issue.claudeCodeProject: Command to register the project management endpoint in Claude Code
issue.commandNote: --scope user registers it for every folder you open Claude Code in (without it, only the folder where you ran the command). This command contains the key. It may stay in your terminal history, so take care on shared screens.
issue.otherClients: Other MCP clients connect to the URLs above with an Authorization header (Bearer followed by the key).

mine.title: My MCP keys
mine.description: Your keys for connecting AI agents (such as Claude Code) over MCP. One key works in every workspace you belong to where your role allows MCP. Keys are never deleted, only expired, and everything done with a key is recorded in the audit log.

empty.ALL: You haven't issued any MCP keys yet

emptyBody.ALL: Issue a key to let an AI agent work on projects and issues with your permissions.
emptyBody.ACTIVE: Issue a key to connect an AI agent. Expired keys are under All and Expired.
emptyBody.EXPIRED: Keys you expired or that reached the end of their period stay here. Keys are never deleted.

admin.title: MCP keys
admin.description: MCP keys of this workspace's members. Expired keys stay as issuance history. A key belongs to its user and also reaches their other workspaces, so this page is view-only; only the owner can expire a key.
admin.blockNote: To block a member's AI agent in this workspace, remove "Work in this workspace with an MCP key" from their roles (switch them to a role without it, or turn it off in a custom role). From the next call, this workspace is invisible to their key.

empty.ALL: Members haven't issued any MCP keys

admin.emptyBody: Keys appear here when members issue them from My MCP keys in their personal settings.
admin.emptyFiltered: Try changing or clearing the filters.

access.title: MCP access log
access.description: Every request that came in with an MCP key — reads, creates, updates, deletes and issue links alike. Only requests made in this workspace are shown, and entries can't be edited or deleted.
access.csvHint: Downloads the filtered result, up to 100,000 rows. The download itself is recorded in the audit log.
access.emptyBody: Entries appear here, one per request, when an MCP key works with this workspace's projects and issues.

detail.title: Access log entry
detail.noWorkspace: None — visible only to the key owner
detail.arguments: Tool arguments summary — long text as length and sha256 only

keyDialog.title: {{name}} — access log
keyDialog.description: Every request made with this key — in all workspaces, including requests that didn't pick a workspace (connect, tool list, rejected).
